--- title: "Orthographic decision" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_DECISION_ORTOGRAFICA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (E · Decision with response time; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_DECISION_ORTOGRAFICA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Decisión ortográfica*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_DECISION_ORTOGRAFICA.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Orthographic decision, from age 6 to 8 (3,399 administrations in 2 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .52. AUC .76–.83 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1937 2039 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 26 (1937) according to the platform | | Task family | E · Decision with response time | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child says which of two options corresponds to the correct orthography of a frequent word. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:-----------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|-------------------------------------------:| | 1937|Decisión ortográfica |Opciones en pantalla; el niño elige | 26| 2|— |180 s |fijo |Aciertos | 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1937.** 2 ejemplos (hueso/ueso, votella/botella) + 26 ítems; límite de 180 s. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1937 · Decisión ortográfica](../../figuras/plataforma/1937.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1937"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Choosing, between two forms that sound the same, the correctly spelled word (for example, *vaca* vs. *baca*) measures **orthographic knowledge**: the representations of specific words in the mental lexicon. This is what allows a word to be recognized at a glance, without converting it letter by letter. **How it is formed.** According to the self-teaching hypothesis, each time the child successfully decodes a new word, something of its written form is stored. Phonological decoding works as an "internal teacher" [@jorm1983recoding]. Computational models show that this mechanism is enough to learn thousands of words and that initial phonological deficits are enough to produce dyslexia [@ziegler2014selfteaching]. A systematic review of 62 experiments confirms the role of phonological recoding in all writing systems [@li2022selfteaching]. It also works in Spanish, except with infrequent spellings of a sound, which need more exposure [@ferroni2014recodificacion]. **What the task measures.** Orthographic choice captures both knowledge of specific words and more general orthographic knowledge. Choosing correctly does not depend only on being able to read the word [@compton2020choice]. In Spanish, the orthographic lexicon contributes to reading competence beyond decoding, and it is refined with years of practice [@cuadro2014lexico]. **What our data show.** 2021 α = .80 and stability between terms ρ = .52, lower than for reading aloud. Even so, it is one of the tasks that best predict low reading fluency years later (median AUC .76, maximum .80). This is to be expected if it measures how many words the child has consolidated, which is precisely what fails in dyslexia in a transparent orthography. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.3| 2039| 2010| 160|2016/17 | 924| 256| 667| 34| | 6.3| 1937| 2011| 193|2017/18 | 670| 0| 670| 30| | 7.1| 1937| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 765| 252| 512| 31| | 7.2| 1937| 2011| 636|2018/19 | 543| 0| 543| 25| | 8.1| 1937| 2010| 638|2018/19 | 497| 154| 342| 25| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 2039| 6.3| 256| 2010| 13.75| 3.37| 13| 0.04| 0.39| 0.00| | 1937| 7.1| 252| 2010| 18.55| 4.11| 19| -0.34| 0.40| 4.76| | 1937| 8.1| 154| 2010| 20.82| 3.96| 21| -0.83| 0.00| 11.04| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Form| Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Warning | |----:|----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------------| | 2039| 6.3| 256|7–21 |0–22 |extreme value: check | | 1937| 7.1| 252|9.5–26 |0–26 |extreme value: check | | 1937| 8.1| 154|9–26 |8–26 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .43–.60 (median .52, 4 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .80. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 6.3| 7.1| 717| 0.60| 0.60| | 2010| 6.3| 8.1| 437| 0.51| 0.48| | 2010| 7.1| 8.1| 445| 0.49| 0.57| | 2011| 6.3| 7.2| 448| 0.30| 0.43| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Reading comprehension (6.3, r = .40); Word and text reading (7.1, r = .51); Word and text reading (7.2, r = .60); Word and text reading (8.1, r = .62). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .76–.83. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .55–.61. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_DECISION_ORTOGRAFICA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .66–.80 (4 time points; 231–486 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|-------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|---:|---:|---:| | 1937| 6.3| 670| 2011| 11.0| 13| 14| 15.0| 17| 20| 23| | 2039| 6.3| 256| 2010| 9.0| 10| 10| 11.0| 13| 16| 19| | 1937| 7.1| 252| 2010| 12.0| 14| 15| 16.0| 19| 21| 24| | 1937| 7.2| 543| 2011| 1.4| 11| 14| 15.5| 20| 23| 25| | 1937| 8.1| 154| 2010| 13.0| 16| 17| 19.0| 21| 24| 26| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_DECISION_ORTOGRAFICA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). If the groups differ, the difference mixes form and cohort. | Time point| Form 1| Form 2|Comparison | d (2 − 1)| SD ratio|Verdict |r between forms |Equating | |----------:|------:|------:|:----------------|---------:|--------:|:----------------|:---------------|:--------| | 6.3| 1937| 2039|different groups | -0.80| 0.88|different scales |— |— | ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.3| 1,594| 0.133| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.3| 1,591| 0.074| 0.139| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.3| 1,587| 0.048| 0.057| |School (ICC) | 6.3| 1,594| 0.080| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 722| 0.210| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 765| 0.017| 0.818| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 764| -0.008| 0.831| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 765| 0.083| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.2| 543| -0.007| 0.864| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.2| 540| 0.099| 0.245| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.2| 538| 0.102| 0.018| |School (ICC) | 7.2| 543| 0.188| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.1| 497| 0.160| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.1| 485| 0.156| 0.085| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.1| 484| 0.036| 0.426| |School (ICC) | 8.1| 497| 0.096| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Orthographic decision” (codes 1937 and 2039; DIS-ESP battery) assesses orthographic knowledge. The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It comprises 26 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 and 2011 cohorts it was administered in 5 sessions, from 6 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .80 (N = 3,922, 26 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 8 months) was ρ = .63 (median of 3 session pairs; range .47–.66). Stability across time points was ρ = .43–.60. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .55–.61. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 6.3 (form 2039), 7.1 (form 1937): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - The task has 2 forms; in 1 of 1 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
